answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using epoch memory-hard proofs bound to each public key. Verifiers broadcast a beacon and run rapid spot-checks over an Argon2 table seeded by the beacon and key. Since tables differ per key, spawning a plume of clones in a nebula of cheap threads forces an attacker to hold dedicated RAM per identity to pass the timing check. However, renting an ocean of cloud memory still scales attacks, and tight timeouts penalize modest hardware.
